# Foundation Requirements Checklist: P-F000 — Foundation

**Purpose**: Validate the requirements quality of spec.md (and cross-check against plan.md) for
the auth flows, session lifecycle, error/Failure taxonomy, and navigation surfaces delivered by
P-F000, before `/speckit-tasks` proceeds.
**Created**: 2026-10-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Auth Flow Requirements (Login / Sign-up)

- [ ] CHK001 - Are client-side validation rules (e.g., password minimum length/format) specified for sign-up and login, or is validation fully deferred to the backend? [Gap, Spec §FR-006, §FR-007, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK002 - Is the UI distinction (if any) between a retryable failure (timeout/offline) and a non-retryable one (invalid credentials, malformed request) specified — e.g., presence or absence of a retry affordance? [Gap, Spec §FR-004, §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is the mechanism for preventing a duplicate account or duplicate session when the app is backgrounded mid-submission specified (e.g., disabling the submit control, idempotent request handling), or left fully to implementation discretion? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK004 - Is "Criar conta" mode's toggle behavior (FR-008) specified as preserving or clearing already-entered field values when switching between login and sign-up? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]

## Session Lifecycle & Expired-Session Overlay

- [ ] CHK005 - Is "usable session" (FR-009) defined precisely enough to distinguish it from "valid," "active," or "renewable," so routing logic is unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK006 - Does the spec specify what "any related background preparation" (FR-010) during the splash state actually consists of, or is this left undefined? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is it disambiguated whether a second session expiry during overlay dismissal causes the existing overlay to remain displayed throughout, versus being dismissed and then re-shown? [Ambiguity, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK008 - Are all elements of "screen state" that must survive the expired-session overlay (FR-013, FR-014, SC-005) enumerated, or is only scroll position given as an example with the rest left to interpretation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013, §FR-014, SC-005]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the approximate duration or threshold for the splash state quantified anywhere in the requirements (vs. only as an implementation-level performance target), so "brief" (User Story 3) is testable? [Clarity, Spec User Story 3, §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK010 - Is the relationship between silent background renewal (Assumptions) and the expired-session overlay (FR-013) consistent — i.e., is it clear the overlay only appears after silent renewal has already been attempted and failed? [Consistency, Spec Assumptions, §FR-013]

## Error / Failure Taxonomy (Either<Failure, T>)

- [ ] CHK011 - Does the spec identify where the authoritative, closed set of backend error codes is defined, given FR-004 and the Backend Failure entity assume a fixed taxonomy? [Traceability, Spec §FR-004, Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK012 - Is the mapping from each of the backend's documented error codes to a specific user-facing message (or message category) specified, or only the general requirement that "every error condition" produce "a clear, non-crashing message" (FR-015)? [Gap, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK013 - For each of the four auth-related calls (sign-up, login, refresh, session-check), are the specific failure modes (timeout, malformed/non-retryable, offline) that requirements expect to be exercised explicitly enumerated, or only described generically via Edge Cases? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases, §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is "retryable flag" (FR-004) requirement's meaning fully specified — i.e., does the spec state what a screen is expected to do differently when a failure is retryable vs. not, beyond showing a message? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]

## Navigation & Placeholder Screens

- [ ] CHK015 - Is the side menu's required destination set (FR-011: Home/Chat, Meus Registros, Configurações) consistent with the Assumptions section's mention of an optional "Planos de Ação" placeholder entry — i.e., is it clear whether that entry's presence or absence affects FR-011's completeness? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK016 - Is "clearly-labeled placeholder" (FR-012) specified with any concrete criteria (e.g., required label text, required "not yet available" indication), or left entirely to implementation judgment? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK017 - Does the spec define what happens if a user attempts an action on a placeholder screen (Meus Registros, Configurações) beyond viewing it — e.g., any inert control feedback — or is "no functional behavior" (FR-012) sufficient to cover all such interactions? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-012, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK018 - Is the requirement that the side menu "overlays the current screen without discarding state" (Acceptance Scenario, User Story 4) distinguished clearly from the separate state-preservation requirement for the expired-session overlay (FR-013), so the two mechanisms aren't assumed to share one implementation requirement? [Consistency, Spec User Story 4, §FR-013]

## Requirement Completeness & Consistency (Cross-Cutting)

- [ ] CHK019 - Is the "if at all" qualifier in FR-016 ("any screen or control belonging to one of them MUST exist only as an inert placeholder, if at all") disambiguated — i.e., does the spec make clear under what condition such a control would legitimately not exist at all? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are the performance thresholds referenced outside spec.md (e.g., <100ms local reflection, >300ms loading-indicator trigger) reflected as a measurable Success Criterion within spec.md itself, or only documented in plan.md's Technical Context? [Consistency, Gap, Spec Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK021 - Does the spec specify whether the loading indicator required for network calls exceeding a latency threshold applies uniformly to all four auth/session calls, or could some calls be exempt? [Gap, Spec Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK022 - Is SC-006 ("zero visual values defined outside the single central source") paired with any requirement for how this is verified (e.g., review process, lint rule), or is verifiability left unaddressed? [Measurability, Spec SC-006]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK023 - Is the assumption that RF03 (biometric/PIN) "is built immediately after this one" validated as a hard dependency, or could delivery-order changes invalidate the routing behavior specified in Assumptions (splash → login/sign-up directly, overlay → login directly)? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK024 - Is the assumption that "every error this unit's calls can return is one of the backend's fixed, documented error codes" validated against an actual enumerated list, or merely asserted without a cross-reference? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK025 - Is the choice of on-device token storage mechanism explicitly scoped as non-normative ("an implementation choice, not fixed by this specification," per Assumptions) consistent with FR-009's requirement that a session "already exists" between launches — i.e., does the spec avoid implying any particular storage guarantee (e.g., survival across app reinstall) that isn't actually required? [Consistency, Spec Assumptions, §FR-009]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (http-client.md,
failure-taxonomy.md, auth-repository.md, session-repository.md), quickstart.md — all present.

**Tests**: Included. `plan.md`'s Constitution Check marks RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) as
"PASS (gate carried into tasks)" and RNF09 requires 15/15 write-endpoint failure scenarios covered
by `mocktail`; `quickstart.md`'s Automated checks run `flutter test --coverage` against a
`lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter. Domain-layer unit tests (`mocktail`) and bloc tests (`bloc_test`)
are therefore generated per story; User Story 4 (pure navigation/presentation, no domain code) has
none, matching the domain-only scope of the gate.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (P1–P5 from spec.md) to enable independent
implementation and testing of each story.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: US1–US5, mapping to spec.md's five user stories
- Exact file paths are given per plan.md's Project Structure

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter app at the repo root: `lib/`, `test/` (plan.md Project Structure; no
`backend/`/`api/` tree — the backend is frozen and consumed only through `docs/input/backend/`).

## Phase 7: User Story 5 - Session expires during active use (Priority: P5)

**Goal**: While a user is active on a screen, the backend session expires; an overlay explains this
and offers re-authentication, after which the user returns to exactly where they were.

**Independent Test**: Force a session-expired response while a screen is in a known state, confirm
the overlay appears over it unchanged, and confirm re-authentication restores that exact state.

### Tests for User Story 5 ⚠️

- [X] T056 [US5] Add to `SessionBloc` bloc_test: an `AuthExpiredDetected` event (raised by any
  authenticated call elsewhere in the app) triggers a silent `refresh()` first; `Right` → stays
  `authenticated`, no overlay-triggering state emitted; `Left` → emits `expiredRenewable` (the
  overlay's trigger state); a second `AuthExpiredDetected` arriving while already `expiredRenewable`
  re-emits `expiredRenewable` rather than proceeding with the stale session (Edge Cases) —
  `test/features/session/presentation/bloc/session_bloc_test.dart` (same file as T042)

### Implementation for User Story 5

- [X] T057 [US5] Extend `session_bloc.dart` with the `AuthExpiredDetected` handling described in
  T056 (same file as T047)
- [X] T058 [US5] Create `lib/features/session/presentation/widgets/session_expired_overlay.dart`: a
  non-dismissible `showDialog` raised through the root `navigatorKey` (T014) whenever `SessionBloc`
  emits `expiredRenewable` — centered card over a light scrim, lock icon, title "Sessão expirada",
  explanatory text, button "Entrar novamente" (research.md R3; prototype-extract.md §2.2) (depends
  on T014, T047, T005, T006)
- [X] T059 [US5] Wire "Entrar novamente" to `context.push` (never `go`/replace) the Login screen on
  top of the current one, so the underlying screen's `State` is never disposed; on a successful
  `AuthBloc` login, pop back to it, dismissing the overlay with the underlying screen's state (e.g.
  scroll position) restored exactly (FR-013/FR-014; User Story 5) (depends on T058, T025/T037, T014)
- [X] T060 [US5] Hook the overlay into the app root — a `BlocListener`/`BlocBuilder` around
  `MaterialApp.router`'s `builder` in `main.dart` watching `SessionBloc` globally, so `expiredRenewable`
  shows the overlay regardless of which screen is currently active (same file as T016) (depends on
  T058)

complete.

## Phase 8: Polish & Cross-Cutting Concerns

**Purpose**: Gate verification across all five stories (quickstart.md Automated checks / Expected
outcome).

- [X] T061 [P] Run `fvm flutter analyze` — 0 issues, and confirm by inspection that no file under
  any `domain/` folder imports `package:flutter` or a class from its feature's `data/` layer (RNF06)
- [X] T062 [P] Run `fvm flutter test --coverage`, extract the `lib/**/domain/**` lcov subset, and
  confirm ≥80% coverage (RNF07); add any missing domain-layer test case needed to close the gap
- [X] T063 Cross-check that all 9 of F000's write-endpoint failure scenarios are covered by
  `mocktail` tests (signup/login/refresh × timeout/malformed-response/no-connection — T019, T031,
  T041), toward RNF09's full 15/15 target across the whole delivery order
- [X] T064 [P] Spot-check every screen this unit ships (Splash, Login/Sign-up, Home/Chat, Meus
  Registros placeholder, Configurações placeholder, Sessão expirada overlay) for any color,
  typography, spacing, or radius value not traced to `design_tokens.dart` (RNF08/Principle IV; not
  yet an automated lint in this unit, per quickstart.md)
- [X] T065 Run quickstart.md's 5 manual/integration validation scenarios end-to-end on an iOS
  simulator/device, confirming every spec.md Acceptance Scenario they map to

---

## Phase 9: Convergence

- [ ] T066 Add a mechanical, automatically-run check (e.g. a `flutter test` that walks `lib/**/domain/**`
  and fails if any file imports `package:flutter` or a class from its feature's `data/` layer, or an
  equivalent script wired into the same `flutter analyze`/CI step quickstart.md already documents) so
  RNF06's "zero layer violations" gate is enforced mechanically rather than only by manual code review —
  `analysis_options.yaml`'s `always_use_package_imports`/`directives_ordering` lints (added in T003) only
  normalize import syntax and do not fail on a domain file importing Flutter or a data/ class per
  Constitution Principle V / RNF06 (partial)

---

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies — start immediately.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup — BLOCKS all user stories.
- **User Stories (Phase 3–7)**: All depend on Foundational completion.
  - US1 (P1) has no dependency on another story.
  - US2 (P2) extends US1's `auth_remote_data_source.dart`/`auth_repository_impl.dart`/`auth_bloc.dart`/
    `login_signup_page.dart` in place — do US1 first.
  - US3 (P3) is independent of US1/US2's files but its splash routes to the Home/Chat page US1
    creates (T028) — do US1 first for a meaningful manual test, though US3's own tasks touch no
    US1/US2 files.
  - US4 (P4) extends US1's `home_chat_shell_page.dart` (T028) — do US1 first.
  - US5 (P5) extends US3's `session_bloc.dart` (T047) and needs US1/US2's login screen as the
    re-authentication destination — do US1 and US3 first.
- **Polish (Phase 8)**: Depends on all five user stories being complete.

### Within Each User Story

- Tests are written first and MUST fail before their matching implementation task.
- Domain entities/interfaces before use cases; use cases before blocs; blocs before pages.
- Data-layer classes (`*_remote_data_source.dart`, `*_repository_impl.dart`) before the
  `service_locator.dart` registration task that wires them in.

### Parallel Opportunities

- All Setup tasks marked [P] (T003, T004) can run in parallel once T001/T002 finish.
- Within Foundational, T005, T007, T009, T011 (and the chain T012→T013) can run in parallel; T006,
  T008, T010 each wait only on their own listed dependency.
- Within each story's test block, tasks against distinct new files are marked [P]; tasks that extend
  a file an earlier story's task already created (e.g. T031/T032/T033, T034/T035/T037/T038) are not
  marked [P] and run after that earlier task.
- US4's tasks (T051–T055) can start as soon as Foundational and US1 (for `home_chat_shell_page.dart`)
  are done, in parallel with US2/US3 work by a different contributor.

---

## Parallel Example: User Story 1

```bash
# Tests for User Story 1 (distinct files, run together):
Task: "Unit test LoginUseCase in test/features/auth/domain/usecases/login_usecase_test.dart"
Task: "Unit test AuthRepositoryImpl.login in test/features/auth/data/auth_repository_impl_test.dart"
Task: "Unit test AuthRemoteDataSource.login in test/features/auth/data/auth_remote_data_source_test.dart"
Task: "bloc_test for AuthBloc login flow in test/features/auth/presentation/bloc/auth_bloc_test.dart"

# Foundational entities needed by US1, also parallel:
Task: "Create Account entity in lib/features/auth/domain/entities/account.dart"
Task: "Create AuthRepository interface in lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/auth_repository.dart"
```

---

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup.
2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (blocks every story).
3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (login → Home/Chat).
4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: run T017–T020's tests, then quickstart.md scenario 1 manually.
5. Demo on a simulator if ready.

### Incremental Delivery

1. Setup + Foundational → foundation ready.
2. US1 (login) → test independently → demo (MVP).
3. US2 (sign-up) → test independently → demo.
4. US3 (splash/launch routing) → test independently → demo.
5. US4 (side-menu navigation) → test independently → demo.
6. US5 (session-expired overlay) → test independently → demo.
7. Phase 8 (Polish) → confirm RNF06/07/08/09 gates and run quickstart.md in full.

### Parallel Team Strategy

1. Team completes Setup + Foundational together (T001–T016).
2. Once Foundational is done, US1 should be finished first (US2, US4, and US5 all extend files US1
   creates). After US1:
   - Developer A: US2 (sign-up, extends US1's auth files).
   - Developer B: US3 (splash/routing — independent of US1/US2's files).
   - Developer C: US4 (side menu — extends US1's Home/Chat page) once US1's T028 lands.
3. US5 starts once both US1 (login destination) and US3 (`SessionBloc`) exist.

---

## Notes

- [P] tasks touch different files with no incomplete dependency.
- [Story] labels map every Phase 3–7 task to its spec.md user story for traceability.
- RNF09's 15/15 write-endpoint scenario target spans the *entire* delivery order (requirements.md
  §12); this unit's tasks close only the 9 scenarios belonging to its own 3 write endpoints
  (signup, login, refresh) — see T019, T031, T041, and the cross-check at T063.
- Every visual value belongs only in `design_tokens.dart`/`theme.dart` (T005/T006) — no later task
  in this file should introduce a literal color, font, spacing, or radius value elsewhere.
- Commit after each task or logical group; stop at any checkpoint to validate a story
  independently.

# Quickstart: validating P-F000 — Foundation

Prerequisites, run commands, and expected outcomes for proving this unit's 5 user stories end to
end. Interface details (headers, URLs, failure types) are in `contracts/`; entity/state details
are in `data-model.md`.

## Prerequisites

- `fvm use 3.47.5` run once at the repo root (installs/links the pinned SDK — see research.md R1).
- `.env` present at the repo root with `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (already exists
  in this repo; never commit it).
- `fvm flutter pub get`.
- A real or simulated iOS device/runner (`fvm flutter devices`), since the target platform is iOS.

## Setup

```bash
fvm flutter pub get
fvm flutter run -d <ios-device-or-simulator-id>
```

## Automated checks

```bash
fvm flutter analyze                                   # 0 issues, incl. no flutter imports under domain/ (RNF06)
fvm flutter test --coverage                            # unit + bloc tests (mocktail, bloc_test)
lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/*/domain/*' -o coverage/domain.info
genhtml coverage/domain.info -o coverage/domain_html    # inspect: >= 80% (RNF07)
```

## Manual / integration validation scenarios

Each maps directly to a spec.md Acceptance Scenario.

1. **Login (User Story 1)**
   - Launch with no stored session → login screen.
   - Enter a valid, existing email/password → lands on Home/Chat.
   - Enter a wrong password → inline, non-crashing error, stays on login screen, can retry.
   - Turn off network, submit → retryable connection-error message, no hang/crash.

2. **Sign-up (User Story 2)**
   - From the login screen, tap the toggle link → title/CTA switch to "Criar conta" (same screen,
     no navigation).
   - Submit a brand-new email/password → account created, lands directly on Home/Chat.
   - Submit an already-registered email → clear error, form stays editable, no crash.

3. **Launch routing (User Story 3)** — exercise all three stored-session conditions:
   - Valid session on device → splash, then straight to Home/Chat, no credentials re-entered.
   - No stored session (fresh install, or after a manual token wipe) → splash, then login screen.
   - Expired-but-refreshable session (manually expire the stored `accessToken`, keep a valid
     `refreshToken`) → splash, silent `auth-refresh`, lands on Home/Chat without any prompt.

4. **Base navigation (User Story 4)** — confirms SC-004 (≤2 taps each way)
   - From Home/Chat, tap ☰ (1 tap) → drawer opens, see Meus Registros, Configurações.
   - Tap Meus Registros (2 taps total) → visible; tap ☰ then Home/Chat (≤2 taps) to return →
     chat shell state (e.g., scroll position) unchanged.
   - Repeat for Configurações, confirming ≤2 taps each direction.
   - Opening the drawer itself visibly scrims the current screen without resetting it.

5. **Session-expired overlay (User Story 5)**
   - Get to a known state on a screen (e.g., scroll Home/Chat partway).
   - Force a session-expired response (e.g., revoke/expire the access token server-side, or stub it
     in a debug build) while that screen is active.
   - Confirm the "Sessão expirada" card appears over a light scrim, screen content still visible
     and unchanged underneath.
   - Tap "Entrar novamente", re-authenticate → overlay dismissed, screen state (scroll position)
     restored exactly.
   - Repeat the forced expiry while the overlay is still visible (before dismissing) → overlay
     persists/reappears rather than letting the user proceed.

## Expected outcome

All 5 scenarios above pass; `flutter analyze` and `flutter test --coverage` are clean; the
`lib/**/domain/**` coverage report meets RNF07; no screen's rendered output uses a color, font, or
spacing value traceable to anything other than `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (spot-check via code
review, since this is not yet an automated lint in this unit).
